land.text: Buenos Aires province, which the Confederation's government lost in the revolt of 11 September 1852 (the Confederation's 1846 outline minus its 1853 outline, as its own dossier writes it)

predecessors.note: The Argentine Confederation dossier (another part) records the same loss in 1852-09 against this slug.

land.text: the whole State, reunified with the Confederation, which became the Argentine Republic

successors.note: Infobox 'Reunification: 12 December 1861', 'Succeeded by: Argentine Republic'; the Confederation dossier records a gain of the province in 1861-12.

correction.text: the State of Buenos Aires, the Province of Buenos Aires as it seceded

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 1: Cliopatria's row begins in 1853 but the page has the State arise from the overthrow of the Confederation government 'in the Province of Buenos Aires on 11 September 1852'; the 1853 outline stands for the last months of 1852. The page defines the territory only 'very vaguely in Article 2' (a claim 'to the foothills of the Andes', Martín García Island).

188,595 km2 for 1853-1856; the page gives no area (only the 1855 census, 248,498 inhabitants), so the infobox comparison is impossible. Unverified beyond the province core: the page is silent on the frontier with the indigenous lands, on Bahía Blanca, Azul and Carmen de Patagones, and on the Andean claim, none of which the outline draws. Page budget: 2 pages.

242,535 km2 for 1857-1859: the outline gains 306 cells (about 54,000 km2) in the south-west pampas (lon -63.5 to -59.8, lat -40.9 to -34.4) over 1853-1856, taken from no neighbour (the Argentine Confederation's shapes do not lose them). Neither page opened dates or places a frontier advance in 1857; kept as drawn, the gain recorded at confidence 1 in the ledger. The Calfucurá page, opened to look for it, is silent too (its only dated item in the window is an attack on Bahía Blanca in 1859). A gap-filler should open the page on the Pampas frontier of the 1850s.

Same outline for 1860. The Pact of San José de Flores (11 November 1859) 'de jure reincorporated' Buenos Aires into Argentina but the infobox keeps the State to the reunification of 12 December 1861 and the Confederation dossier has Buenos Aires outside until then.

correction.text: the 1860 outline carried through 1861 until the reunification of 12 December 1861

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1860, the infobox ends the State on 12 December 1861 ('Buenos Aires rejoined the Argentine Confederation after the former's victory at the Battle of Pavón in 1861').

region.text: the State of Buenos Aires, the Province of Buenos Aires as it seceded

ledger.note: 11 September 1852: Buenos Aires overthrows the Confederation's government and secedes. The State 'resulted from the overthrow of the Argentine Confederation government in the Province of Buenos Aires on 11 September 1852' (infobox 'Established: 11 September 1852'); its constitution was sanctioned on 11 April 1854 (promulgated the 12th; infobox 12 April).

region.text: the city of Buenos Aires and the country round it, besieged by Lagos

ledger.note: 1 December 1852: Colonel Hilario Lagos besieges Buenos Aires. Lagos 'on 1 December, initiated the Siege of Buenos Aires', which 'continued through June 1853'; the year 1852 is implied by the page, not printed.

region.text: the city of Buenos Aires and the country round it

ledger.note: 12 July 1853: Urquiza calls off the siege. 'Urquiza called off the siege on 12 July' after the commander of his blockading flotilla was bribed on 20 June.

region.text: the south-west pampas that the 1857 outline holds and the 1853 outline does not

ledger.note: 1857: the south-west pampas appear inside the State's outline. Cliopatria adds about 54,000 km2 (306 cells) in 1857; neither page opened dates or places any advance of the frontier, so the event rests on the shape (page silent).

region.text: the Cañada de Cepeda, north of Pergamino, in the north of the State

ledger.note: 23 October 1859: the Confederation defeats Buenos Aires at Cepeda. 'The Battle of Cepeda of 1859 took place on October 23' at Cañada de Cepeda, north of Pergamino, where Urquiza's Confederation army 'defeated the State of Buenos Aires forces' under Mitre.

region.text: the Cañada de Cepeda, north of Pergamino

ledger.note: 11 November 1859: the Pact of San José de Flores. 'On November 11, on the mediation of' Francisco Solano López of Paraguay, the two sides signed the pact, which 'de jure reincorporated' Buenos Aires into Argentina with 'certain privileges' (the page gives no year but the battle's, 1859); the State stays separate in fact until 1861.

region.text: the field of Pavón on the Santa Fe side of the Paraná, near Rosario

ledger.note: 1861: Mitre's army fights the Confederation at Pavón. The page: 'Buenos Aires rejoined the Argentine Confederation after the former's victory at the Battle of Pavón in 1861' (the page gives no day; 17 September 1861 is the date in the Argentine Confederation dossier from another page).

region.text: the field of Pavón near Rosario
the whole State of Buenos Aires

ledger.note: 12 December 1861: Buenos Aires returns to the Confederation, which becomes the Argentine Republic. Infobox 'Ended: 12 December 1861 (reunification)', 'Succeeded by: Argentine Republic'.

12 December 1861: the State of Buenos Aires ends and its land passes to the Argentine Confederation, now the Republic. Mitre, governor 1860-1862, 'continued to serve as governor of the Buenos Aires Province after the reunification'.

wars.name: Siege of Buenos Aires (1852–1853)
wars.outcome: The siege fails: Lagos's besiegers lose the Confederation's blockading flotilla to bribery (20 June 1853) and Urquiza calls off the siege on 12 July 1853; Buenos Aires stays separate.
wars.note: The page prints no year for the start; 'continued through June 1853' puts the start in 1852.

wars.name: Battle of Cepeda (1859)

zones.text: the Cañada de Cepeda north of Pergamino

wars.outcome: Confederation victory on 23 October 1859 under Urquiza over Mitre; the Pact of San José de Flores of 11 November reincorporated Buenos Aires de jure, with privileges.
wars.note: The page names no frontier changes.

wars.name: Battle of Pavón (1861)

zones.text: Pavón, on the Santa Fe side near Rosario

wars.outcome: Buenos Aires wins at Pavón in 1861 and rejoins the Confederation; reunification is dated 12 December 1861.
wars.note: The State of Buenos Aires page gives the battle only as 'in 1861' and cites no article; no Pavón page was opened within the page budget.

certainty.note: The State's territory was 'defined very vaguely' (Article 2: to the Andean foothills); the southern and western frontier with the indigenous lands is approximate throughout; the northern line with the Confederation (Santa Fe, Córdoba) and the Uruguay line along the river are better known but no page opened gives them.

sources.title: Calfucurá
sources.note: Opened to look for the south-west frontier advance of 1857: silent on treaties, forts and any frontier change in 1852-1861; its only dated item in the window is the 1859 attack on Bahía Blanca. Nothing used.

notes: Cliopatria's row ends in 1860 but the page (infobox) keeps the State to 12 December 1861; new keyframes for 1852 (secession in September) and 1861 carry the outline there. Not settled with two pages: (1) the 1857 enlargement of 306 cells in the south-west pampas is on no page opened (confidence 1 gain from nobody); (2) the Pavón date (17 September 1861) is not on the State page; (3) the page says nothing on the frontier with the indigenous lands, on Martín García Island's status in the shape, or on any Uruguayan line; (4) the 1860 constitutional reform and the Convention of 1860 are not on either page. The Argentine Confederation dossier (another part) has the matching loss in 1852-09 and gain in 1861-12 with this slug as counterpart, and keeps Buenos Aires out of the Confederation to 12 December 1861, as this dossier does; Cliopatria's Confederation 1861 shape contains the province from 1861. The Siege of Buenos Aires and Pavón contest zones are radii because the pages give places, not areas. Page budget: 2 pages, plus a third (Calfucurá) opened for the 1857 enlargement and found silent.
